differences: HueSync exact product mapping supplies APEX HID_V2 identity; no new model or family alias is admitted.

HueSync gen_cmd emits a Linux 64-byte command. HC Windows V2 color helpers and IDevice.WithReportID establish report ID 0 plus a 64-byte command, totaling 65 bytes. Linux bytes alone do not establish a Windows descriptor.
Brightness thresholds and ties-even rounding come from HueSync set_led_color whole-update; gen_brightness supplies the explicit enabled field and levels 1/3/4.
The reviewed consumer sets enabled=(percent>0). HueSync whole-update currently forces enabled=True and Disabled mode to solid black; that workaround is not claimed equivalent or copied here.
HC SendV2Brightness always encodes enabled=1 and a clamped level 0..4. Its zero encoding is not used as an off command and is not equated with the HueSync discrete mapping.
Off requests percent=0 and explicitly sends enabled=0 with the HueSync low level 1; the encoded level byte is not zero. No cached color or serial status/preset is used.

Brightness/enable is completed before a300ms wait and color/mode; this follows HueSync whole-update processing timing, preserving cancellation and owner rechecks. Solid copies RGB directly twenty times; rainbow consumes mode03; second color and custom speed are unavailable.
The existing frozen APEX declaration and X1 serial method provenance remain intact. Only its effective lighting consumer is replaced.
Runtime native ownership and managed transport must both validate the exact current endpoint and 65-byte output descriptor. Software source admission does not assert a physical effect.
